svg.title: Desiccant dryer controller — protoboard layout (logic 90×70 mm, relay 70×50 mm)
svg.text: Desiccant dryer controller — protoboard layout (proposal)
Top view, component side; wiring on the underside. Left: logic + 24 V board, 90 × 70 mm. Right: mains relay board, 70 × 50 mm. Only a 4-wire logic-level harness links them.
Prints 1:1 at 100 % (the SVG is sized in mm; 6 px/mm on screen): check the 10 mm bar measures 10 mm before using it as a drilling guide.
LOGIC + 24 V BOARD (7 × 9 cm)
RELAY BOARD (5 × 7 cm)

g.text: ANTENNA — keep copper, parts, wires out

svg.text: VALVE A ← GPIO11
(drain, load −)
VALVE B ← GPIO10
(drain, load −)
FAN ← GPIO6
(drain, load −)
24 V IN
Each MOSFET channel: 100 Ω gate, 10 kΩ gate → GND, IRLZ44N (marking face toward viewer,
legs down: G D S; tab = drain), 1N4007, band (cathode) → 24V+, anode → drain. Valve/fan
ESP placement: vertical along the left edge,
antenna end at the top edge, USB-C at the
bottom edge, Qwiic cable exits left.
* PN2222A or P2N2222A? CHECK THE MARKING BEFORE FITTING
Flat face toward the bottom of this drawing (toward the mains terminals):
PN2222A is E B C, P2N2222A is C B E. They are mirror images and both are sold
as a TO-92 “2N2222”, so the marking on the part is the only way to tell. The
wrong way round swaps collector and emitter: the stage never switches and the
base–emitter junction breaks down near 6 V. Read every part before it goes in
and rotate a P2N2222A 180°. Bulk TO-92 leads are 1.27 mm pitch; this footprint
is 2.54 mm (the formed-lead PN2222ATA/ATF and P2N2222ARL1G).
Mains side (relay board)
L → COM; the contact wired to “L sw” is NO. Identify NC first: with the coil
unpowered, NC has continuity to COM. NC is live whenever the heater is off; leave it
unconnected. The relay switches L only; N passes through.
COM is at the coil end: 6.3 mm centre to centre from each coil pad, ≈4 mm pad edge to
pad edge. The PN2222A / 1N4007 stage sits ≥ 3 hole rows (7.62 mm) from COM, NO and NC.
Relay pads are off the grid (datasheet, mm: COM (0, 0), coil (2.0, ±6.0), NO/NC (14.2,
±6.0), 1.3 mm holes). Nearest grid fit: rows ±6.35, columns 12.7 apart, COM 2.54
outboard (≈0.35–0.5 mm splay per pin). Drawn at the real positions: coil and NO/NC
pins sit 0.35 mm inside hole columns 12.7 mm apart, and COM falls on the centreline
between two columns, so drill its hole there. COM/NO/NC are 1.0–1.1 mm flat blades:
ream those three holes to ≥ 1.2 mm.
Earthing: PSU FG → PE. Chassis, enclosure and heater sheaths bond to PE at a star
point that is NOT on this board. 0 V bonds to PE at one point at the PSU, because the
relay’s 1500 VAC coil–contact rating is basic insulation only. Fuse T 3.15 A in L at
the inlet, ahead of the PSU and heaters.
Each heater’s switched L lead carries a one-shot thermal fuse (TCO) between “L sw” and
the heater — the only protection against a welded contact. The fuses ordered trip at
133 °C: clamp them to the pack body next to the DS18B20, NOT to the heater sheath,
which runs far hotter and would open one on the first cycle. A TCO holds at roughly Tf
− 15–25 °C, i.e. near the 120 °C firmware latch, so check the datasheet and keep the
firmware limit below it. ≥ 2 A / 250 VAC, crimped leads.
Before wiring real heaters: make the four heater/valve switches internal: true
(CLAUDE.md open item).

Build order (logic board)
Before fitting J-USB or the ESP: power the 24 V input, set the MP1584 module’s trimmer to 5.00–5.10 V
measured at the buck OUT+ pad (the Schottky and J-USB are downstream of it), lock the pot, power down. A
fixed-5 V module avoids the trimmer.
Fit parts; check every net against the net list in docs/hardware.md with a meter before the ESP goes in.
Keep every copper feature out of the antenna keep-out.
J-USB and USB-C
The ESP’s USB pin is the USB-C VBUS net, with no diode or fuse, feeding D2 (BAT20J) → AP2112 3.3 V LDO
(600 mA, 6.5 V abs. max) and the MCP73831 charger (7 V abs. max). The MP1584 is non-synchronous and cannot
sink current, so a higher host VBUS simply stops it switching. The hazard with J-USB fitted and a USB
cable plugged in is the buck, if above the host’s VBUS, sourcing current into the computer’s port, up to
the MP1584’s 4–4.7 A current limit.
The series Schottky (SS34 or 1N5819) from buck 5 V to J-USB does NOT block that: buck → USB pin is its
forward direction, which is how the board is powered. It blocks a host from back-feeding the buck output,
the 5 V bus and the relay coils, for 0.3–0.4 V; with the buck at 5.0 V the LDO still keeps ≥ 0.39 V
dropout margin at the 430 mA peak (BAT20J and AP2112 worst-case drops).
So J-USB, not the diode, keeps the buck off a computer’s port: pull it before plugging in a USB-C cable,
every time. Keep the buck ≤ 5.1 V; a USB-C host may also refuse to attach while VBUS is pre-biased. Being
safe with J-USB fitted would need a real power path (ideal-diode / load-switch ORing), not a series diode;
that is not in this layout.
Harness and off-board
Harness: JST-XH 4-way, B4B-XH-A on each board, XHP-4 housings, 1:1 cable: 1 = 5 V, 2 = GND, 3 = GPIO13
through 1 kΩ (heater A), 4 = GPIO12 through 1 kΩ (heater B). The 1 kΩ base resistors sit at the logic-
board end; the 10 kΩ pull-downs stay on the relay board. The relay board carries no 24 V. XH pitch is 2.50
mm (0.12 mm short of 0.1" over four pins).
Display on the enclosure front via the 8-pin 1:1 cable; keep the cable under 15 cm (ESPHome ili9xxx runs
40 MHz SPI by default; set data_rate: 20MHz in display-st7789.yaml if the image tears). Header order
follows LCDWIKI/QDtech MSP1541-style modules; Waveshare’s 1.54" module is VCC GND DIN CLK CS DC RST BL.
BLK must drive an on-module transistor (check BLK → VCC ≈ 10 kΩ unpowered); a bare LED anode would
overload GPIO17.
SHT45 on the ESP’s Qwiic connector. 24 V PSU → 24 V IN. Three DS18B20 cables → the green block, each probe
on its own 3V3 / DQ / GND triple.
Caveats (numbers from docs/datasheets/, see its README)

ESP geometry is verified from SparkFun’s Eagle files (mcu/sparkfun-esp32-s2-thing-plus.brd/.sch and the dimension drawing): PCB 64.77 × 22.86 mm, rows 20.32 mm apart and ending 12.70 mm before the antenna

end, 16-pin pin 1 (EN) 13.97 mm and 12-pin pin 1 (BAT) 24.13 mm from the USB end, Qwiic at the USB end on the 12-pin edge, mounting holes only at the USB end. Component side up with USB-C at the left, the

12-pin row is on top. The USB-C shell’s width is drawn approximately; only its centring and 1.1 mm overhang are from the files. The antenna (last 6.3 mm) is at the board’s top edge; USB-C face 3.2 mm inside
the bottom edge.
The buck module footprint (22 × 17 mm, pad positions) is UNVERIFIED: “MP1584 mini” boards vary by vendor. Measure the one you have before drilling. Don’t cut metal from this drawing.

PN2222A, flat face toward viewer: E B C (P2N2222A is C B E — check the datasheet of the part you have). Drawn at 2.54 mm pitch; bulk TO-92 parts are 1.27 mm (the formed-lead PN2222ATA/ATF and P2N2222ARL1G
are 2.54 mm). Here the flat face points toward the mains terminals.

Relay pads are the only intentional exceptions to the grid. Alternative, not chosen: take the contacts off the protoboard, with screw-terminal relay sockets or an off-the-shelf 2-channel 5 V relay module
fed from 3V3 with its JD-VCC jumper removed.
Bare bus wire runs along hole rows and never crosses another bare bus; insulated hookup wire may cross anything. Mains wiring on the relay board is insulated wire rated for 120 VAC.
Open items (questions for review)

Creepage: two empty rows are 5.6 mm pad edge to pad edge, and undrilled plated pads between mains and logic reduce it further; a cleared band or slot along the boundary, or contacts off the protoboard, is
needed.
The 24 V input has no reverse-polarity protection, fuse or bulk input capacitor.
No hardware over-temperature cutout backs up the firmware if a relay contact welds; check what the original Azco board/packs provided.
Stock DS18B20 probe leads are rated under 100 °C and the SMC VDW22 valve is rated 50 °C, both on a 90 °C pack; verify or change parts.
